<!-- proofline:finding-series=01a202ca-dd98-70fe-9060-f302d5ae49ae -->
**Warning** · History skips deliveries tied at a page boundary

The cursor stores only `scheduled_at`, so the next page excludes deliveries with the same timestamp but a smaller `id`.

Operators never see those deliveries when paging through history.

Encode both `scheduled_at` and `id` in the cursor and resume using the same descending order as the query.

[View finding in Proofline](https://proofline.sh/orgs/by-id/01a202a0-cd61-7684-99bc-53c775b0de50/reviews/01a202ca-2a38-711a-ad74-f9565dfa4344/findings/01a202ca-dd9c-760b-997f-5cbfb7c5bf7c)

Also at:
- [`migrations/001_initial.sql`](https://github.com/Pratik8445/bench-run-proofline/blob/b42257746fa78caad922340082a2a27ed00cdeb8/migrations/001_initial.sql#L1-L8) lines 1 to 8
- [`reports.py`](https://github.com/Pratik8445/bench-run-proofline/blob/b42257746fa78caad922340082a2a27ed00cdeb8/reports.py#L23-L29) lines 23 to 29

findings.body:
<!-- proofline:finding-series=01a202ca-dd9b-711e-8bcd-8fb47c9e8429 -->
**Warning** · Small history pages now scan the entire deliveries table

This change orders history by `scheduled_at DESC, id DESC`, which the shipped schema cannot serve from an index.

A first page now visits every row and does sorting work instead of stopping after `limit + 1` primary-key rows.

Add a migration creating an index on `deliveries(scheduled_at DESC, id DESC)`.

[View finding in Proofline](https://proofline.sh/orgs/by-id/01a202a0-cd61-7684-99bc-53c775b0de50/reviews/01a202ca-2a38-711a-ad74-f9565dfa4344/findings/01a202ca-dda4-74fa-8d93-3ca7b37c3688)
